message.content:
Review: The problem is clearly framed as a causal follow-up to the target study, and it distinguishes the reported mechanism from what the supplied aggregate data can establish. It specifies the system, key observables, proposed interventions, comparison conditions, onset rule, and run-level unit of analysis. The central question is understandable: does changing coarsening alter the onset or persistence of temporal order, or do both respond to the drive independently?

Feedback: Clarify how “robust subharmonic time-crystalline order” will be operationalized: specify the frequency band or peak-selection rule, how neighboring frequencies define the reference level, and how finite-time effects and the drive period enter the metric. The preregistered threshold and required number of cycles are appropriately identified as design choices, but should be set before data collection. Also define the coupling manipulation and how it will be verified to change coarsening without unintentionally changing other system properties. The proposed controls help address alternatives, though a drive-only control may not fully separate direct drive effects from interactions between drive and coupling. Finally, state how runs will be randomized or matched and how uncertainty will be estimated; the supplied aggregate export alone cannot answer the question, so synchronized raw signals and repeated runs are necessary.

Rating (1-5): 4
